thread:
alex: Heads-up — I'm going to land a small terraform change to HPA and Karpenter provisioner annotations in the next PR. Goal: reduce churn during scale-down and avoid evicted pods getting stuck in GC. Planning to add the ttl-after-finished and the karpenter.k8s.aws/ttl-not-ready annotations.
tanya: Quick Q — does the change touch any secret paths (service account or IRSA) or just k8s manifests/annotations? Want to know if I need to rotate any IAM roles in the Dedicated clusters.
alex: Only annotations + HPA target tweaks. No secret changes. The terraform patch updates the k8s_manifest resources in infra-k8s module, not the aws_iam_role resources. Will paste the snippet in a sec.
samir: Can you include the rationale in the PR description? We had that long tail of Pending pods last week when nodes terminated; adding TTL should make Karpenter cleanup faster. Also remind QA to watch the pod eviction metrics: `kube_pod_status_phase{phase="Pending"}` and node termination events.
alex: Yep, PR will have the before/after metrics and a `kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp` sample. Snippet of the terraform manifest I plan to apply:

```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "karpenter_provisioner" {
  manifest = yamldecode(<<YAML
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: default
  annotations:
    karpenter.sh/ttl-after-empty: "30m"
    karpenter.k8s.aws/ttl-not-ready: "15m"
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: "node.kubernetes.io/instance-type"
    operator: Exists
YAML
  )
}
```

marta: For HPA, what are the new targets? We need to make sure the VPA (we run a permissive VPA in some namespaces) won't immediately try to inflate requests and confuse autoscaling.
alex: Changing CPU target from 60% -> 55% for the inference-worker HPA, and adding an annotation to ignore VPA: `vpa.kubernetes.io/update-mode: "off"` on that deployment. That should stop any conflict.
tanya: Sounds fine. One more check: terraform plan output will list the `kubernetes_manifest` update only, right? If it tries to replace the Provisioner resource we might get pod disruptions.
alex: Correct, plan shows `~` (update) not `-/+` replace. Here's the plan snippet I got locally:

```
  # kubernetes_manifest.karpenter_provisioner will be updated in-place
  ~ resource "kubernetes_manifest" "karpenter_provisioner" {
      id = "default"
      manifest = {...}
    }
```

samir: Can you add a canary rollout in Karpenter's annotations to reduce blast radius? e.g. set `karpenter.sh/scale-down-disabled: "true"` on a single provisioner first, observe for an hour, then flip on the rest.
alex: Good call. I'll add a `scale-down-disabled` toggle to the PR with instruction to flip after 1h monitoring. Also will add a smoke test checklist in the PR template: check `eviction_restarts`, `pending_pod_age`, and `node_termination_events` metrics.
marta: If you're touching TTLs, please also add a note to the ops runbook about how `karpenter.sh/ttl-after-empty` interacts with our PDBs and drain timeouts. We hit an edge case where PDB blocked deletion and TTL expired but GC didn't catch up.
alex: Will do. I'll update the runbook and ping SRE to sanity-check the PDB interaction. 
deploy-bot: Deploy check: terraform plan succeeded for infra-k8s (module.k8s_manifest.karpenter_provisioner: plan ok) — no secrets modified. :white_check_mark:
tanya: Thanks — I'll do a quick review once you open the PR. If it looks clean we can schedule the apply during the 02:00-04:00 maintenance window and have SRE on standby.
alex: PR opened: https://git.company/infra/terraform/compare/PR-432 — brief description + monitoring checklist. Tagging @tanya @samir for reviews. :thumbsup:
samir: Reviewing now, will post lgtm or comments within 30m.
